concepts.name: Formation of NSO: Merger of CSO and NSSO
key_dimensions: Year of merger (2019) and the administrative order under which it was constituted
Distinction between the legacy roles of CSO (Central Statistics Office) vs NSSO (National Sample Survey Office) before merger
Which functions were retained, restructured, or renamed post-merger
UPSC trap: Confusing NSO with MOSPI — NSO is a subordinate office under MOSPI, not a separate ministry

concepts.name: NSO's Structural Position within MOSPI
key_dimensions: Hierarchical relationship: NSO under Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
Distinction between NSO, MOSPI, and the National Statistical Commission (NSC) — three separate entities often confused
Role of the Chief Statistician of India and their dual charge as Secretary of MoSPI
UPSC trap: NSC is an advisory body; NSO is the operational/field arm — different mandates

concepts.name: National Statistical Commission (NSC): Composition and Mandate
key_dimensions: Statutory vs non-statutory status of NSC — it is a non-statutory body set up by cabinet resolution (2005), not by an Act of Parliament
Composition: Chairperson + 4 members with fixed tenure, appointed by the President
Advisory role: NSC advises government on statistical standards but cannot enforce compliance
UPSC trap: NSC is NOT the same as NSO; NSC does not collect data — it sets standards and resolves disputes between ministries on data

concepts.name: GDP Estimation Methodology and NSO's Role
key_dimensions: NSO as the sole official agency for releasing GDP/GVA estimates in India
Three approaches: Expenditure, Income, and Production/Output — which one India primarily uses (Expenditure-side with GVA as primary)
Base year revisions: Shift from 2004-05 to 2011-12 base year and its controversies
UPSC trap: GVA + Net Taxes on Products = GDP at Market Prices — direction of the formula is frequently tested

concepts.name: GDP Advance Estimates vs Revised Estimates: Release Calendar
key_dimensions: First Advance Estimate (FAE): Released in January before the fiscal year ends — used for Union Budget preparation
Second Advance Estimate, First Revised Estimate, Second Revised Estimate — sequential release timeline
Why advance estimates are inherently provisional: limited data availability for Q3 and Q4
UPSC trap: The Union Budget uses FAE of current year, not the previous year's final estimate

concepts.name: National Accounts Statistics (NAS) and the System of National Accounts (SNA)
key_dimensions: India follows the UN System of National Accounts (SNA 2008) — international framework for GDP computation
What NAS covers: GDP, GNP, NNP, National Income, Per Capita Income — hierarchy and interrelationships
Transition from factor cost to market price as primary reporting basis (post-2015 revision)
UPSC trap: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA) — sign of NFIA matters; India typically has negative NFIA

concepts.name: Consumer Price Index (CPI): NSO's Role in Compilation
key_dimensions: NSO compiles CPI (Rural, Urban, Combined) — released monthly; used as headline inflation measure by RBI
CPI vs WPI: NSO handles CPI; Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT) handles WPI — different ministries
Base year of CPI: 2012 = 100; items in basket and weights (food & beverages carry ~45% weight)
UPSC trap: RBI uses CPI (Combined) for inflation targeting under the Flexible Inflation Targeting framework, NOT WPI

concepts.name: Index of Industrial Production (IIP): Compilation and Significance
key_dimensions: IIP is compiled by NSO and released monthly with a 6-week lag
Base year: 2011-12 = 100; three sectors — Mining, Manufacturing, Electricity with respective weights
Use-based classification within IIP: Primary goods, Capital goods, Intermediate goods, Infrastructure/Construction goods, Consumer durables, Consumer non-durables
UPSC trap: IIP measures volume/quantum of industrial output, NOT value — it is a volume index, not a price index

concepts.name: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS): Design and Metrics
key_dimensions: PLFS launched in 2017 by NSO to replace the earlier quinquennial Employment-Unemployment Survey (EUS)
Two reference periods: Usual Status (one year) and Current Weekly Status (CWS) — what each captures
Key metrics: Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Unemployment Rate (UR)
UPSC trap: PLFS is annual for rural + urban; quarterly reports cover only urban areas — frequency differs by geography

concepts.name: Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES): Gaps and Recent Revival
key_dimensions: Last completed and published survey: 2011-12; the 2017-18 survey results were withheld/not released officially
HCES data used for: poverty estimation, CPI basket revision, national accounts private consumption estimates
2022-23 HCES: Conducted and results released in 2024 — key findings on consumption inequality
UPSC trap: HCES is NOT the same as PLFS; HCES measures spending patterns, not employment — often conflated in questions

concepts.name: Annual Survey of Industries (ASI): Scope and Limitations
key_dimensions: ASI is conducted by NSO under the Collection of Statistics Act, 2008; covers factories registered under Factories Act
Coverage threshold: Factories using power with 10+ workers OR without power with 20+ workers
Key data outputs: GVA from manufacturing, employment in organised manufacturing, capital formation
UPSC trap: ASI covers only the ORGANISED manufacturing sector — informal/unorganised manufacturing is NOT captured by ASI

concepts.name: Collection of Statistics Act, 2008: Legal Framework for NSO Operations
key_dimensions: The Act empowers the Central Government to collect statistics on any matter of public interest
State governments can collect statistics on state subjects; concurrent application in concurrent list subjects
Penalties for non-compliance and provisions for confidentiality of data provided by respondents
UPSC trap: The Act does NOT make it mandatory for individuals to respond in ALL surveys — specific notification required to make a particular survey mandatory

concepts.name: Informal Sector Estimation: NSO's Methodological Challenge
key_dimensions: NSO uses 'enterprise approach' for unorganised sector — estimates based on NSSO enterprise surveys and labour surveys
Benchmark-Indicator method: Unorganised sector GDP estimated using benchmark (survey year) and extrapolated with indicators
Criticism: Post-demonetisation GDP estimates faced scrutiny over adequacy of informal sector capture
UPSC trap: India's GDP includes unorganised sector estimates — it is NOT measured only from formal/registered establishments

concepts.name: NSO and Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Monitoring
key_dimensions: NSO designated as the nodal agency for compiling India's SDG National Indicator Framework
Coordination role: NSO collates data from line ministries and state governments for SDG reporting to UN
Challenges: Data gaps, frequency mismatches, and absence of disaggregated data at sub-national levels
UPSC trap: NITI Aayog releases the SDG India Index (ranking states), while NSO provides the underlying statistical framework — different roles

concepts.name: Back Series GDP Data Controversy (Pre-2011 Base Year Estimates)
key_dimensions: NSO constituted an advisory committee to compute back series data using 2011-12 base year methodology
Released back series (1993-2012) in 2018 showing higher growth rates than earlier CSO series — triggered controversy
Methodological dispute: NSC members and external economists disputed the approach, leading to advisory committee disbandment
UPSC trap: The back series is an ESTIMATE using new methodology, not actual historical data — distinction between revision and recomputation

concepts.name: Price Indices Compiled by NSO vs Other Agencies: Mapping and Overlaps
key_dimensions: NSO: CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined), IIP — MoSPI umbrella
DPIIT (under Commerce Ministry): WPI (Wholesale Price Index) and its sub-indices
RBI: No primary price index; uses NSO's CPI for monetary policy — consumers vs producers price tracking
UPSC trap: There is NO single 'Producer Price Index' officially adopted in India yet — WPI serves as a proxy, and India is in process of transitioning

concepts.name: Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) vs NSO Poverty Data
key_dimensions: NITI Aayog releases India's National MPI using NFHS data (not NSO survey data directly)
Official poverty line in India was last estimated by Tendulkar Committee (2011-12) using HCES data from NSO/NSSO
Rangarajan Committee (2014) proposed a revised poverty line — never officially adopted
UPSC trap: India does NOT currently have an officially updated poverty line post-2011-12 — absence of 2017-18 HCES data created the gap

concepts.name: Gross Capital Formation (GCF) and Investment Statistics by NSO
key_dimensions: GCF = Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF) + Change in Stocks + Valuables — NSO compiles all components
GFCF as a % of GDP: Key indicator for investment climate; tracked separately for public, private, and household sectors
NSO distinguishes between Gross and Net Capital Formation (Net = Gross minus Consumption of Fixed Capital/depreciation)
UPSC trap: Household sector GFCF in India includes construction by households (own homes) — it is NOT purely corporate investment

concepts.name: Statistical Federalism: Centre-State Data Coordination Mechanisms
key_dimensions: State Directorates of Economics and Statistics (DES) are the state-level counterparts coordinating with NSO
Steering Committee on Statistics and the Conference of Central and State Statistical Organisations (COCSSO) as coordination forums
State GDP (GSDP) is estimated by respective State DES using NSO methodology — NSO does not directly compute GSDP
UPSC trap: GSDP estimates are released by STATE governments, not by NSO — NSO only issues national aggregates and methodology guidelines

concepts.name: Data Quality, Independence, and Credibility Concerns around NSO
key_dimensions: Institutional independence debate: NSO/NSC lack statutory independence comparable to RBI or CAG — subject to executive pressure
Specific controversies: Suppression of HCES 2017-18, back series GDP dispute, PLFS data release delays
International comparisons: IMF, World Bank, and UN have noted concerns about data quality and timeliness in India
UPSC trap: NSC was set up by cabinet resolution (non-statutory) — its recommendations are advisory and the government is NOT legally bound to accept them
